title: RULES for the Hotel Breakfast Room Before It Opens #shorts
description_hook: You couldn't sleep, so you went down early. The hotel breakfast room is fully set, every light is on, and nobody is there yet. A work of fiction.

lines.say: You go down to breakfast early. Nobody's here. Rule one: the coffee pours by itself. Let it finish.
lines.img: an empty hotel breakfast room at dawn, rows of set tables under bright ceiling lights, a coffee machine on the counter filling a white cup by itself, steam rising

lines.text: SKIP THE TABLE SET FOR YOU
lines.say: Rule two. Don't sit where a single place is already set.
lines.img: a small square table in an empty breakfast room with a single neatly set place, folded napkin, polished cutlery, a chair pulled out slightly, every other table bare

lines.say: Rule three. If the muted TV shows weather for a town you don't know, leave.
lines.img: a muted wall-mounted television glowing in an empty hotel dining room, its screen showing a blurred map of an unfamiliar coastline in soft colors, cereal dispensers below

lines.say: Rule four. Never take the last waffle. It isn't yours.
lines.img: a lone golden waffle under a glass warmer lid on a stainless steel buffet counter, juice machines humming beside it, fluorescent light on empty trays

lines.say: Rule five. The guest book has today's date. Don't sign it.
lines.img: an open guest book with a pen resting in its spine on a hotel front counter, blank lined pages, a small brass bell beside it, empty lobby beyond

lines.say: Breakfast starts at six. The clock says 5:59. It said that when you walked in. The coffee is pouring again.
lines.img: a plain round wall clock with no numerals above an empty breakfast buffet, the hands frozen just before the hour, pale dawn light at the windows

loop_back: The clock never moved, so it is still the moment you walked in: the coffee machine starts pouring again, which is rule one.

gumi.say: So. Which rule would you break first?
